result:
I'd make high-quality education and critical thinking universally accessible and effective for every person, from early childhood onward.

So many of the world's hardest problems—poverty, conflict, poor health, environmental damage, inequality—are downstream of gaps in knowledge, skills, and the ability to reason clearly about evidence and trade-offs. Widespread, genuine education wouldn't magically fix everything, but it would give far more people the tools to understand their circumstances, cooperate across differences, innovate, and hold institutions accountable. It compounds: better-educated societies tend to be healthier, more prosperous, more stable, and better at solving the next set of problems.

That's the single change I'd pick, because it multiplies human capacity rather than just treating one symptom.
